thayer-entries.title: A Greek-English Lexicon of the New Testament (Thayer), by entry
thayer-entries.author: C. L. W. Grimm & C. G. Wilke, tr./rev./enl. Joseph Henry Thayer (1889)

scheme.honesty: entries INFERRED from OCR; not proofread; ids provisional until segmentation is ruled on
scheme.note: 5,486 entries inferred from the page OCR of 699 body pages, against the ~5,600 Thayer's really has. Rule: line-initial Greek headword, kept only on the max-weight alphabetical chain and only if paragraph-initial or a Strong's lemma (see convert_thayer_entries). 3,964 candidates dropped as out of alphabetical order, 112 in order but with no other evidence. A real entry the rule missed is not lost: its text is inside the entry before it. Every unit links to the page(s) of the page book `thayer` it was cut from, which is the checkable citation. 335 entries open on a headword OCR misread (one letter off, or in Latin lookalikes) and read back to the one Strong's lemma it can be: lex.headword keeps the OCR, lex.headword_read the reading. 157 more open where a SECOND OCR (pipeline/ocr_thayer2.py, the original JP2 scans) prints a Strong's headword the first OCR lost; only the boundary is taken from it, never a word of the text. The appendix pages after the last entry are not part of any entry. 5,092 entries linked to strongs-greek by headword (accents ignored); 14 matched more than one Strong's lemma and are left unlinked with the candidates under lex.strongs_candidates.

wycliffe-earlier.title: The Wycliffite Bible, the earlier version (c. 1382) (Forshall and Madden 1850)
wycliffe-earlier.author: John Wycliffe and his followers; ed. Josiah Forshall and Frederic Madden

scheme.citation: Book.chapter.verse in the Clementine Vulgate's numbering (F&M number as the Vulgate); ids not linked to kjv: units, each unit's `kjv` resolves it
scheme.honesty: verse numbers decoded from the margin OCR of the 1850 scans; each unit says how its number was got (scan.number: read as printed, read with a letter-for-digit fix, inferred from the sequence, or 'heading' for a chapter's first verse, which follows its heading unnumbered); a verse that begins mid-line is split at a sentence break, a guess flagged in scan.start; the manuscripts' collation letters stay glued to the words they mark and the yogh is the OCR's '3'; text is unproofread OCR. Coverage of the Clementine's verses is measured per book (measure.books); a book below the bar is given by scan leaf, not by verse. A verse number decoded twice keeps both units, the second as '<id>~2' (then ~3...) with scan.duplicate_number and no kjv: a house convention shared with the Charles books, awaiting Adam's ruling
